==English==

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:resisten}}
From {{inh|en|enm|resisten}}, from {{der|en|frm|resister}} and {{der|en|fro|resistre}}, and their source, {{der|en|la|resisto|resistere}}, from {{m|la|re-}} + {{m|la|sisto|sistere|cause to stand}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ɹɪˈzɪst/|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/ɹɪˈzɪst/|/ɹəˈzɪst/|a=SSB,GA,CA,AU}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-resist.ogg|a=California}}
** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Simplificationalizer-resist.wav|a=New Jersey}}
** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Grendelkhan-resist.wav|a=Connecticut}}
* {{IPA|en|/ɹəˈzəst/|a=NZ}}
* {{hyph|en|re|sist}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɪst|s=2}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[attempt]] to [[counter]] the [[action]]s or [[effect]]s of.
#* {{quote-video game|en|developer=w:BioWare|title={{w|Mass Effect (video game)|Mass Effect}}|location=Redwood City|publisher=Electronic Arts|year=2008|genre=[[science fiction|Science Fiction]]|system=PC|scene={{w|Citadel (Mass Effect)|Citadel}}|isbn=9780784546642|oclc=246633669|passage=Shepard: You could have '''resisted'''. You could have fought! Instead, you surrendered. You quit.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-06-28|author=w:Joris Luyendijk
|volume=189|issue=3|page=21|magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly
|title=[http://www.guardian.co.uk/commentisfree/joris-luyendijk-banking-blog/2013/jun/19/banking-britain-beyond-control Our banks are out of control]
|passage=Seeing the British establishment struggle with the financial sector is like watching an alcoholic who still '''resists''' the idea that something drastic needs to happen for him to turn his life around.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[withstand]] the actions of.
#* {{quote-book|en|author=w:Charles Johnstone|title=The Reverie; or, A Flight to the Paradise of Fools|url=http://books.google.com.sg/books?id=1mAzAQAAMAAJ&pg=PA202|volume=2|location=Dublin|publisher=Printed by Dillon Chamberlaine|year=1762|page=202|oclc=519072825|passage=At length, one night, when the company by ſome accident broke up much ſooner than ordinary, ſo that the candles were not half burnt out, ſhe was not able to '''reſiſt''' the temptation, but reſolved to have them ſome way or other. Accordingly, as ſoon as the hurry was over, and the ſervants, as ſhe thought, all gone to ſleep, ſhe ſtole out of her bed, and went down ſtairs, naked to her ſhift as ſhe was, with a deſign to ſteal them {{...}}}}
#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=16|passage=The preposterous altruism too!{{...}}'''Resist''' not evil. It is an insane immolation of self—as bad intrinsically as fakirs stabbing themselves or anchorites warping their spines in caves scarcely large enough for a fair-sized dog.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[oppose]]; to refuse to accept.
#: {{syn|en|hold out}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To be distasteful to.
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Pericles|II|iii|text=These cates '''resist''' me,}}

====Usage notes====
* This is a [[catenative]] verb that takes the ''gerund (-ing)''. See [[Appendix:English catenative verbs]].
